setup.database: PostgreSQL 18.7 (postgres:18 container drizzle-bench-tuned), aarch64 Linux VM on a Mac, --cpus 4, 4 GB memory
setup.dataset: orders (n rows: customerId (n%20000)+1, orgId (n%100)+1, status by n%5, paid n%2=0, createdAt evenly over 7 years to 2026-11-01, reference ORD-00000001) and customers (20,000 rows)
setup.client: single client, one connection per request, medians of 10 runs (5 when a scenario takes over 1 s, 3 over 20 s), warm cache
setup.engineNote: snapshot of drizzle-resource packages/core at that commit, read only; the engine on main has no capped count, so capped counts are hand SQL

profileDefinitions.out-of-the-box: schema ord_*: primary keys, orders (createdAt, id), orders (customerId), trigram on lower(orders.reference) and lower(customers.name)
profileDefinitions.tuned: out-of-the-box plus customers (name) and orders (createdAt desc, id asc). Landing values are the engine page statement (count none) plus a capped count (limit 10001) by hand SQL, summed
profileDefinitions.scoped: tuned plus orders (orgId, createdAt, id), resource scoped to orgId = 42 (query.scope), 1% of rows

notes: PROVISIONAL: this machine was never quiet. Every run was taken at one-minute load average 4 to 10 for the runs kept here (my own benchmark adds about 4 to 5 of that; other threads add the rest). Each chosen run's load is in setup.chosenRuns; high_load is true above 8. A final quiet run is planned and will replace these numbers.

Landing rule for tuned: every count-bearing request = the engine's page statement (tuned indexes, count: none) + a capped count (select count(*) from (select 1 ... limit 10001) t) by hand SQL, summed. The engine on main has no capped count. Raw tuned engine runs with an exact count (names without the landing/ prefix) are kept for reference only and must not be used as tuned values.
Out of the box landing values are the engine run end to end with its exact count.
verdict: ratio = out-of-the-box median / tuned median. improved above 1.1, worse below 0.9, unchanged between, or when the difference is under 0.3 ms.

worse: search-rare-reference-plus-count and search-rare-customer-plus-count at 1M and 10M. With count none the engine plans a rare search as an index walk on the sort index (RFC: 515 ms class of problem), so its page part is slower than the whole out-of-the-box request, whose exact-count path is fast. Do not show them as improvements.

Sort by customer name: landing/sort-customer-name-plus-count is the customers(name) index only variant; landing/sort-customer-name-denormalized-plus-count copies the name onto orders (orders.customerName, index (customerName, id)) and sorts by the root column. The index alone improves 1.3x at 10M; the copy improves by hundreds of times.

Facets: landing/two-root-facets and landing/four-mixed-facets in tuned use the fastest measured of GROUPING SETS (what the engine does) and one statement per facet, each sequential on one connection and concurrent on 3 connections. Field 'all' has the four numbers, 'uses' the winner, requiresEngineChange true when the winner is separate statements, onTodaysEngine the GROUPING SETS concurrent number (the engine runs its facet statement groups with Promise.all, so on main GROUPING SETS on 2 connections is what it does; a group with one facet is already a plain single-column statement), verdictOnTodaysEngine its verdict. The engine's own end to end number is the out-of-the-box value; the hand GROUPING SETS pair is a mirror of it and can differ by tens of percent. Facets are hand SQL through node-pg, not the engine.

Scenario names changed with the dataset: three-root-facets became two-root-facets (status, paid), five-mixed-facets became four-mixed-facets (status, paid, customer.segment, customer.name). The old consumption-table runs are superseded and kept in results/superseded-consumption/.

Data artifacts of the specified formulas: createdAt grows with id, so createdAt order equals id order and a mixed-direction cursor (createdAt desc, id asc) is cheap even without the tuned index (deep-cursor-id-asc about 0.5 ms at 10M out of the box). orgId, status and paid are all functions of n, so inside tenant 42 every order has status 'paid' and paid = false: scoped facets have one value each.

Scoped profile = tuned schema plus index (orgId, createdAt, id), engine scope orgId = 42 (100k rows at 10M). Exact count inside the tenant is cheap (landing/page-plus-count-exact); the capped variant is landing/page-plus-count.

Methods: engine = through the drizzle-resource engine with pg Pool over TCP; hand-sql = psql \timing inside the container (counts) or node-pg (facets); engine+hand-sql = sum of both medians (p95 is also a sum, so only a rough bound).
Hand counts and the page-only twins were measured at lower load than the full engine runs; compare them with that in mind.
